Manhattan browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive fuzz browse by enclosure pedal Manhattan Fuzz Unit Published on July 7, 2014 Manhattan fuzz pedal picture by Electric Warrior picture by Electric Warrior picture by Electric Warrior picture by Electric Warrior Information The Manhattan Fuzz Unit is an OEM version of the mid-1970s Sola Sound Jumbo Tone Bender circuit, built in the United Kingdom and distributed under various brand names including B&M Champion Fuzz, G.B. Fuzz Unit, CMI Fuzz Unit, and West Wood Fuzz Unit. Produced by Sola Sound (Colorsound) for third-party labels, it shares identical electronics with these companion models, differing only in finish and branding. The circuit is a silicon-based fuzz design derived from the Electro-Harmonix Big Muff but modified with one fewer gain stage and minor component value changes. This alteration produces a distinctive fuzz character that combines the saturated sustain of a Big Muff with tighter low-end focus and a more open midrange. The Manhattan Fuzz Unit delivers thick, harmonically rich distortion that remains articulate, with a smooth top end and long sustain. Its voicing makes it effective for both guitar and bass, and it became known for its strong, singing tone and dynamic response. The pedal is housed in a folded and stamped steel enclosure characteristic of Colorsound and Sola Sound units of the period, featuring bright painted finishes such as orange or silver with simple screen-printed labeling. Internally, original examples use period-correct components including Zetex ZTX series transistors and Mullard tropical fish capacitors. Like other models in the series, it was built with handwired construction on a stripboard layout. Controls Volume: Adjusts the overall output level Tone: Balances the frequency response between low and high emphasis Sustain: Controls the amount of gain and sustain Connections 1/4-inch input and output jacks 9V battery operation (no external power jack on original units) Technical Specifications Circuit type: Three-stage silicon fuzz, based on the Jumbo Tone Bender topology Transistors: Typically Zetex ZTX or BC109 silicon devices Construction: Handwired stripboard assembly Enclosure: Stamped steel housing with painted finish Power: 9V battery only Highlights OEM variant of the Sola Sound Jumbo Tone Bender circuit
